newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline AOM boosts Los Angeles service.
newsitem.headline: French airline AOM boosts Los Angeles service.

text.p: An upgrading of AOM France Airlines' DC-10-30 passenger service from Paris to Los Angeles and French Polynesia will boost freight capacity and service on the route, its cargo director Bernard Tetu told Reuters.
"From June 30, we will be adding a fifth weekly Paris-Los Angeles-Papeete (Tahiti) frequency and this will provide more scope to develop the U.S. west coast as a cargo destination," Tetu said.
Because of the priority given to Papeete-bound freight, AOM has only been loading an average of two tonnes of freight per week for Los Angeles, Tetu added.
"With the extra frequency, we should be able to increase this to 10 tonnes per week," he said.
The DC-10-30 can carry around 12 tonnes of freight per flight on this routeing.
AOM said it will also upgrade its Paris-Colombo-Sydney-Noumea (New Caledonia) DC-10-30 passenger service from one to two weekly frequencies, effective June 29.
"This upgrade is welcome news for freight too," Tetu said
AOM is the only airline to offer a direct link between Paris and Australia.
